title: Aethelflaed | A New Opera
description:
Aethelflaed is a bold, 90 minute, fully staged opera that tells the epic story of the Battle of 910AD in which Queen Aethelflaed led her army to victory against the Vikings. Sung in Old English and performed by five principal singers, chorus, and a full orchestra, the opera fuses the grandeur of traditional opera with a modern sonic edge.

This Autumn, Aethelflaed | A New Opera will embark on a tour through some of the UK’s most historic sacred spaces with an intimate evening of music, storytelling, and history. Blending live operatic performance with historical commentary and multimedia presentation, the tour explores the remarkable life of Queen Aethelflaed, the warrior ruler who led her people against Viking invasions in 910AD.

Performed by soprano Rachel Kobernick with commentary by composer Andre Fratto, each event offers audiences a rare behind-the-scenes look at the creation of a new opera sung in Old English and inspired by both grand opera tradition and cinematic spectacle. Featuring excerpts from the score, discussions of Anglo-Saxon history, and insights into the opera’s development, the tour is designed to be engaging for seasoned opera lovers, history enthusiasts, and first-time audiences alike.

Set against the atmosphere of cathedrals and historic venues across England, the recital tour serves as the first public chapter in the journey toward the opera’s fully staged world premiere.
address: St Philip's Cathedral, Cathedral Square, Colmore Row, Birmingham, B3 2QB

title: Cathedral Choir Concert – A Foretaste of Christmas
description:
This short free concert offers a foretaste of Advent and Christmas to mark the opening of the Cathedral Christmas Market.  The music will lead us from Advent through to the threshold of Christmas, a mix of familiar and less familiar choral gems, getting us in the mood for Christmas but leaving us wanting more. 

The cathedral’s professional choir of boys, girls and lower voices will be conducted by David Hardie and accompanied on the organ by Conor McGlone. 

The programme will include choral music looking towards Christmas by Handel, Elizabeth Poston, John Rutter, David Willcocks and others.

Admission is by donation on the door in aid of the Cathedral Music Fund.    

No Booking is required.

title: Gore Lecture: Reflections from Corrymeela by The Reverend Shona Bell
description:
About Gore Lecture

Our sixth annual Gore Lecture in Public Theology will be presented by The Reverend Shona Bell on ‘Reflections from Corrymeela’.

Our annual Gore Lecture builds on the vision of the first Bishop of Birmingham, Charles Gore – who believed strongly in social justice. Our speakers will tackle challenging topics and we explore Public Theology together. There will be a time for questions after the main presentation, and the lecture will be livestreamed on our YouTube channel.

Everyone is welcome to join this FREE event in the cathedral and online. Please register for tickets below.

The Reverend Shona Bell is a priest, mediator and conflict transformation practitioner whose work spans 30 years both nationally and internationally. Her work has focused on civic leadership, post-conflict violence normalization, and peace process sustainability. Shona served as Programme Manager for Sectarianism at the Corrymeela Community, supporting individuals and communities navigating religious, political, and social divisions. Her practice is grounded in dialogue, relationship-building, and the possibilities for transformation in deeply divided societies. As a member of Corrymeela she helped lead a national ritual of reconciliation and has a particular interest in the role ritual can play in social healing. Shona is currently a Priest in the Church of Ireland bringing together faith and peace building as a member of the Corrymeela Community.

title: THE MUSIC OF MOTOWN AT CHRISTMAS
description:
XPERIENCE LIVE presents The Music of Motown at Christmas in a stunning candlelit setting at Birmingham Cathedral

Monday 7th December 2026 | Doors: 6.00pm | Show: 6:30pm–7:45pm | Last entry: 6:25pm

Monday 7th December 2026 | Doors: 8:15pm | Show: 8:45pm–10:00pm | Last entry: 8:40pm

Step into a winter wonderland of soulful magic as the timeless hits of Motown are brought to life in this spectacular candlelit Christmas celebration. Set against the warm glow of flickering candlelight, this amazing concert promises an unforgettable night of music and holiday spirit.

Be swept away by the unmistakable sound of Motown as world-class singers and an incredible live band take to the stage, performing all the greatest hits from legendary artists such as The Temptations, Stevie Wonder, Jackson 5, The Supremes, Smokey Robinson, Marvin Gaye, Four Tops, Diana Ross, Gladys Knight & many more. With soaring vocals, lush harmonies and the irresistible rhythms that defined a generation, this show will have you clapping, dancing and singing along from start to finish.

From the uplifting energy of dancefloor anthems to the heartwarming soul classics that touch the spirit, every song is delivered with passion and festive flair. Whether you’re reliving treasured memories or discovering these iconic songs for the first time, this is the perfect way to celebrate the most wonderful time of the year.

So gather your friends and loved ones, dress up for a night of sparkle, and immerse yourself in the soulful sounds of Motown at Christmas – a truly magical evening that will fill your heart with festive cheer.
address: St Philip's Cathedral, Cathedral Square, Colmore Row, Birmingham, B3 2QB

title: Viennese Christmas Spectacular by Candlelight
description:
Programme

Strauss II – Overture to Die Fledermaus
Strauss II – Tritsch-Tratsch-Polka
Shostakovich – Waltz No. 2
Sibelius – Valse triste
Tchaikovsky – Waltz from The Sleeping Beauty
Korngold – Serenade from The Snowman
Lehár – ‘Meine Lippen, sie küssen so heiß’ from Giuditta
Suppé – ‘Hab’ ich nur deine Liebe’ from Boccaccio
Strauss II – ‘Laughing Song’ from Die Fledermaus
Tchaikovsky – Selections from The Nutcracker, including Pas de deux
Lehár – ‘Vilja-Lied’ from The Merry Widow
Strauss II – ‘Csárdás’ from Die Fledermaus
Strauss II – The Blue Danube

Artists

Sofia Kirwan-Baez Soprano

About

This programme celebrates the elegance, charm and sheer joy of the Viennese tradition with a dazzling selection of orchestral and vocal favourites.

At its heart is the music of Johann Strauss II, the “Waltz King”, whose works capture the wit, sparkle and irresistible energy of 19th-century Vienna. From the effervescent Die Fledermaus Overture to the playful Tritsch-Tratsch Polka, literally “chit-chat” or “gossip”, culminating in The Blue Danube, one of the most famous waltzes ever written: an unofficial anthem of Vienna and a piece that has enchanted audiences for generations, from grand ballrooms to the silver screen in 2001: A Space Odyssey.

Alongside Strauss, the programme explores the many moods of the waltz, from Shostakovich’s jazz-infused Waltz No. 2 to the haunting beauty of Sibelius’s Valse triste. Tchaikovsky brings a touch of magic with the graceful Waltz from The Sleeping Beauty and the much-loved Nutcracker Suite, with some of the most recognisable music ever written — from the delicate sparkle of the “Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy” to the sweeping beauty of the “Waltz of the Flowers”.

The programme also shines a light on the golden age of operetta, with soprano favourites including Lehár’s Meine Lippen, sie küssen so heiß and Vilja, Suppé’s Hab’ ich nur deine Liebe from Boccaccio, and two sparkling moments from Die Fledermaus: Adele’s famous Laughing Song and the fiery Csárdás. Korngold’s Serenade from The Snowman adds a note of nostalgic warmth to this richly coloured programme.

Full of elegance, nostalgia and exhilarating musical colour, this is a concert to lift the spirits and delight audiences of all ages.

title: Nutcracker Suite and Rachmaninov 2nd Piano Concerto at Christmas by Candlelight
description:
Step into the warm glow of candlelight this festive season and experience the magic of Christmas through the timeless beauty of classical music, set within the enchanting surroundings of Birmingham Cathedral.

This special festive concert features a sparkling programme of much-loved classical masterpieces, including selections from Tchaikovsky’s enchanting Nutcracker Suite, Rachmaninov’s deeply romantic Piano Concerto No. 2, and a joyful traditional festive medley guaranteed to capture the spirit of the season.

Performed by the acclaimed Piccadilly Sinfonietta with renowned concert pianist Warren Mailley-Smith, this captivating Christmas performance promises an evening of elegance, warmth, and festive celebration. With over 200 performances each year, the ensemble — featuring some of the UK’s finest classical musicians — has become a beloved presence on the British classical scene, celebrated for its vibrant and expressive interpretations of the great classical repertoire.
